newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power down due to mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power down due to mild weather.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. eased Tuesday amid balmy temperatures throughout much of the region as well as lower spot natural gas prices, market sources said.
"Loads are down because of the weather, but we also think people are caught up on (natural gas) storage," said an Arizona utility trade souurce.

According to Weather Services Corp, the western U.S. will see above normal temperatures this week. Precipitation is also expected to be above normal, except in the Southwest, where near normal levels are expected.
Power generation was deemed ample, with the Bonneville Power Administration continuing to offer surplus power during both peak and off-peak hours.
The Salt River Project's 720 MW unit 1 at the Navajo power plant in Page, Ariz., was shut Saturday and is scheduled to return to operation December 18.
Next-day firm, on-peak power at the Palo Verde substation in Arizona was last quoted $20.00-21.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), down from $21.00-22.00 before the long holiday weekend.
Four Corners was also quoted $21.00-22.00, compared with $21.50-23.00.
Next-day California-Oregon border (COB) power seen at $22.75, compared with quotes at $23.00-24.00 for Monday and Tuesday.
Cash COB for December was last quoted $22.80-23.15, compared with $23.20-23.75. December Palo Verde was quoted $20.75-21.30, compared with $21.40-22.20.
